messages.subject: unexpected output from compiled nimbleFunction
parts:
Hello nimble users and developers,

Thanks very much for all your hard work building and maintaining nimble. I recently ran into some issues trying to use the "RW_llFunction_block" sampler, and I think I tracked the issue back to something having to do with the way my nimbleFunction for the log-likelihood is written to C++ and compiled. When I run the following minimal example, the compiled and uncompiled versions of llFun$run() give different answers. The compiled version is not what I'd expect to get.

library(nimble)
code <- nimbleCode({
  A[1:2, 1:2] <- diag(2) * 2
})
Rmodel <- nimbleModel(code)
llFun <- nimbleFunction(
  setup = function(model) { },
  run = function() {
    A <- model$A
    A_inv <- nimArray(0, c(2, 2, 2))
    A_inv[1, 1:2, 1:2] <- inverse(A[1:2, 1:2])
    returnType(double(2))
    return(A_inv[1, 1:2, 1:2])
  }
)
RllFun <- llFun(Rmodel)
RllFun$run()
CRll <- compileNimble(RllFun, Rmodel)
CRll$RllFun$run()

I noticed that if I change the order of the indices and replace A_inv[1, 1:2, 1:2] with A_inv[1:2, 1:2, 1] in both places it occurs, then I seem to get the right output.

Can you help me see what I'm missing?

Thanks very much for your help,
Henry Scharf

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: unexpected output from compiled nimbleFunction
parts:
Hi Henry,

Thanks for narrowing this down to a simple reproducible case.  This is a bug.   I think it has to do specifically with Eigen (C++ library) placing the solution to a matrix inverse into a map (a matrix not in contiguous memory due to indexing).  I note that for operations other than inverse, the code works, e.g if solve(A[1:2, 1:2]) is replaced with 2*A[1:2, 1:2].

Here is a workaround:

llFun <- nimbleFunction(
  setup = function(model) { },
  run = function() {
    A <- model$A
    A_inv <- nimArray(0, c(2, 2, 2))

(I'm not sure if you will really use larger objects, so just mentioning that for larger objects, using init=FALSE in nimArray, if you don't need the zeros as initial values, can be somewhat faster.)

-Perry

parts: Thanks, Perry! I'll keep the init=FALSE argument in mind.

On Monday, December 7, 2020 at 8:10:19 AM UTC-8 pdevalpine wrote:
Hi Henry,

Thanks for narrowing this down to a simple reproducible case.  This is a bug.   I think it has to do specifically with Eigen (C++ library) placing the solution to a matrix inverse into a map (a matrix not in contiguous memory due to indexing).  I note that for operations other than inverse, the code works, e.g if solve(A[1:2, 1:2]) is replaced with 2*A[1:2, 1:2].

llFun <- nimbleFunction(
  setup = function(model) { },
  run = function() {
    A <- model$A
    A_inv <- nimArray(0, c(2, 2, 2))

    A_inv[1, 1:2, 1:2] <- B

    returnType(double(2))
    return(A_inv[1, 1:2, 1:2])
  }
)

-Perry
